# Does full-text availability move the mechanism ranking?

*Generated by `scripts/census_oa_bias.py` over 4,403,994 MeSH-indexed census articles, of which 936,347 (21.3%) carry a PMC identifier. Both arms use the SAME expert descriptors; the split is defined by PMC identifier presence.*

The split measures **PMC identifier presence**, a proxy for full-text availability. This scan does not verify current access, an open-access licence, or a local full-text copy. The historical JSON field names `with_fulltext` and `oa_rate` retain this proxy meaning.

Mechanism names follow `mesh-mechanism-map.yaml` and inherit its descriptor scope. In particular, `sonodynamic` selects the broad `Ultrasonic Therapy` descriptor, including general ultrasound therapy. This group does not isolate sonodynamic therapy; its identifier rate and median year describe the broader descriptor group.

The superseded version of this test compared 4,830 full-text records against 5,586 abstract-only ones, with the full-text side 98.7% open access. That is not a contrast. Here the split is 936,347 against 3,467,647.

**3 of 16 mechanisms shift 3 or more positions** between the two arms. PMC identifier rate runs 18.4% (`sonodynamic`) to 63.5% (`mrna-vaccine`), against 21.3% for the census as a whole.

Equal counts share a competition rank (for example, 1, 1, 3). Zero counts tie below observed mechanisms within a populated arm; an arm with no mapped observations has no ranking.

**The confound is in the last column and is not controlled here.** Identifier coverage may reflect publication era as well as subject and access. Read each identifier rate alongside its median year where dates are available. This comparison does not separate these effects or quantify an era contribution; it cannot attribute a ranking difference to access.
